title: FedEx Expands China Logistics Network with New Guangzhou International Cargo Terminal, Strengthening Asia Pacific and Global Trade Connectivity
summary: New facility enhances connectivity between China's Greater Bay Area, Asia Pacific, and global markets, helping businesses access faster, smarter, and more resilient supply chains
body_markdown:
**SINGAPORE, November 16, 2026** — Federal Express Corporation (FedEx), one of the world’s largest express transportation companies, today announced the official opening of the FedEx Guangzhou Baiyun Airport International Cargo Terminal 4 (the “International Cargo Terminal”), a major investment that strengthens connectivity between China’s Greater Bay Area (GBA), Asia Pacific, and global markets. Developed in collaboration with Guangdong Airport Authority, the new facility expands logistics capacity, enhances cross-border trade capabilities and helps businesses access faster, more efficient connections to new global markets.


The opening marks another milestone in the company’s long-term commitment to China and its continued investment in the infrastructure, technology and network capabilities that enable regional and international trade. Working alongside the FedEx Asia Pacific Hub at Guangzhou Baiyun International Airport, the new cargo terminal strengthens FedEx’s integrated air network and expands connectivity between South China and key markets across Asia, Europe, the Middle East and the Americas. Following the facility launch, shipment volumes handled by FedEx through Guangzhou are expected to grow, improving access to global markets for customers across the region.


The approximately 45,000 square meter facility integrates warehousing, sorting operations and customs supervision within a single air cargo complex. Designed to support both express parcels and freight shipments, it significantly expands FedEx operational connectivity in South China and international markets for customers across one of the world’s most important manufacturing and trading regions.


The facility’s intelligent sorting system can process up to 28,000 shipments per hour at peak capacity, more than tripling previous processing capability, while annual cargo handling capacity exceeds 100,000 metric tons. For customers, this means greater network capacity, faster shipment processing and enhanced access to international markets. Businesses across sectors including manufacturing, e-commerce, healthcare, cold chain logistics and high-value technology industries will benefit from improved connectivity and more resilient supply chain solutions.


The Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area has emerged as one of the world’s leading centers for manufacturing, innovation and international trade. In the first three quarters of 2026, the region’s nine mainland cities recorded imports and exports of US$ 1.26 trillion, accounting for 21% of China’s total trade\[1\]. As businesses increasingly seek to diversify markets and strengthen supply chain resilience, demand continues to grow for logistics infrastructure that can seamlessly connect South China to the rest of the world.


“The future of trade depends on reliable connectivity, resilient supply chains, and access to global markets,” said Salil Chari, president, Asia Pacific, FedEx. “The Greater Bay Area remains one of the most dynamic economic regions in the world, and this investment reinforces our commitment to helping businesses in China and across Asia-Pacific grow internationally. By strengthening connectivity and integrating this facility into our global network, we are enabling customers to move goods more efficiently, reach new markets, and seize emerging opportunities in global trade.”


The International Cargo Terminal also showcases the company’s continued investment in digital innovation and intelligent logistics. Advanced technologies including artificial intelligence, automation, and Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) improve operational efficiency, shipment visibility, and processing accuracy. These capabilities support businesses seeking more agile, data-driven supply chains and enable FedEx to maintain sorting accuracy above 99%. A smart customs-supervised warehouse, supported by digital documentation, pre-declaration, and intelligent alert systems, further reduces clearance times for customers.


Additionally, the facility incorporates energy-efficient features including natural daylighting, smart lighting systems and green landscaping. Electric forklifts, charging infrastructure and intelligent energy management systems further support the company’s efforts to reduce its environmental impact while maintaining operational excellence.


**About Federal Express Corporation**
FedEx Corp. (NYSE: FDX) provides customers and businesses worldwide with a broad portfolio of transportation, e-commerce, and business services. With annual revenue of $90 billion, the company offers integrated business solutions utilizing its flexible, efficient, and intelligent global network. Consistently ranked among the world’s most admired and trusted employers, FedEx inspires its more than 450,000 employees to remain focused on safety, the highest ethical and professional standards and the needs of their customers and communities. FedEx is committed to connecting people and possibilities around the world responsibly and resourcefully, with a goal to achieve carbon-neutral operations by 2040.
